from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Warm-up: The Geometric View of a Matrix", 
                          ["Matrices are functions that transform vectors.", 
                           "Imagine a plane transforming under a matrix.", 
                           "The unit square moves to a parallelogram."])
        
        # Define objects
        plane = Axes(x_range=[-2, 4], y_range=[-2, 4], axis_config={"include_tip": True}).scale(0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(plane, 'C3')
        
        i_hat = Vector([1, 0], color="#FF0000")
        j_hat = Vector([0, 1], color="#00FF00")
        
        # Start vectors
        self.add(plane)
        self.add(self.place_at_grid(i_hat, 'C3'), self.place_at_grid(j_hat, 'C3'))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#0000FF"))
        # Show transformation matrix logic (simulated by a box)
        rect = Rectangle(width=1.5, height=1.5, color="#0000FF")
        self.place_at_grid(rect, 'C3')
        self.play(Create(rect))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        
        # New vectors
        i_hat_new = Vector([1, 1], color="#FFFF00")
        j_hat_new = Vector([-1, 1], color="#FFFF00")
        
        self.place_at_grid(i_hat_new, 'C3')
        self.place_at_grid(j_hat_new, 'C3')
        
        self.play(Transform(i_hat, i_hat_new), Transform(j_hat, j_hat_new))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Matrix multiplication BA represents this composition.",
            "We apply B to the columns of A.",
            "This maps the transformation steps perfectly.",
            "The product BA simplifies sequential movement.",
            "This is the beauty of matrix algebra."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The 'Aha!' Moment: Matrix Multiplication", lecture_lines)
        
        # Setup visual elements
        square = Square(side_length=1, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(square, 'C2')
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(FadeIn(square))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        transformed_square = square.copy().set_color("#00FFFF")
        transformed_square.apply_matrix([[1, 1], [0, 1]]) # Example matrix B
        self.play(Transform(square, transformed_square))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        transformed_square_2 = square.copy().set_color("#FF00FF")
        transformed_square_2.apply_matrix([[1, 0], [1, 1]]) # Example matrix A
        self.play(Transform(square, transformed_square_2))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.play(Indicate(square))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Visual Synthesis: The Sequential Path", [
            "Watch the vector move through two transformations.",
            "First it changes under A, then B.",
            "The matrix BA performs both at once."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        v = Vector([1, 1], color=YELLOW)
        v_label = MathTex(r"\vec{v}", color=YELLOW, font_size=24)
        
        # Setup objects
        vec_group = VGroup(v, v_label).shift(LEFT * 1.5)
        self.place_at_grid(vec_group, 'C2', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.play(FadeIn(vec_group))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF00FF")
        
        v_prime = Vector([2, 0.5], color=BLUE)
        v_double_prime = Vector([0.5, 2], color=RED)
        
        self.play(Transform(v.copy(), v_prime), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(Transform(v.copy(), v_double_prime), run_time=1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        final_v = Vector([0.5, 2], color=GREEN)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(v, final_v), run_time=2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Closing: Why Order Matters", [
            "Order matters: AB does not equal BA.",
            "Rotating then scaling changes the result.",
            "Scaling then rotating creates a different pose."
        ])
        
        # Define base shapes (using Square for representation)
        shape_a = Square(side_length=1.5, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.5)
        shape_b = Square(side_length=1.5, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.5)
        
        self.place_at_grid(shape_a, 'C2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(shape_b, 'C5', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(Write(shape_a), Write(shape_b))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        # Rotating then scaling: Rotate shape A
        self.play(Rotate(shape_a, angle=PI/4))
        self.play(shape_a.animate.scale(0.5))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        # Scaling then rotating: Scale shape B then rotate
        self.play(shape_b.animate.scale(0.5))
        self.play(Rotate(shape_b, angle=PI/4))
        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: Matrix Multiplication as Composition of Linear Transformations

sections.title: Prerequisite Warm-up: The Geometric View of a Matrix
sections.content: Define a matrix not just as a grid of numbers, but as a function. A matrix A transforms a vector v into a new vector Av. Visualize this as a transformation of the 2D plane (e.g., rotation, scaling, or shearing).
sections.example: Visualize a 2x2 matrix transforming the unit square (defined by vectors i and j) into a parallelogram.

sections.title: Defining Composition: One Step After Another
sections.content: Introduce the concept of applying two transformations sequentially. If transformation A is applied first, then B is applied to the result, we denote this as B(Av).
sections.example: Imagine a cat icon on a grid: First, matrix A rotates the cat 90 degrees; then, matrix B doubles its size. The final position is the result of applying B(A(v)).

sections.title: The 'Aha!' Moment: Matrix Multiplication
sections.content: Explain that matrix multiplication (BA) is defined precisely to represent this composition. The columns of the new matrix BA are the results of applying the second transformation B to the columns of the first transformation A.
sections.example: Show the calculation steps clearly: The result of applying B to the transformed basis vectors of A creates the columns of the new matrix BA.

sections.title: Visual Synthesis: The Sequential Path
sections.content: Animate the 'Path of a Vector': A vector v moves under A, then the resulting vector moves under B. Show that the single matrix BA achieves this movement in one jump.
sections.example: A robotic arm movement: Matrix A shifts the arm segment, and Matrix B adjusts the gripper. Show that multiplying the matrices creates a single 'master' transformation that tracks the final state instantly.

sections.title: Closing: Why Order Matters
sections.content: Conclude by highlighting non-commutativity (AB ≠ BA). Use the physical intuition: rotating then scaling a shape is often different from scaling then rotating it.
sections.example: Use a character (e.g., a 'Game Sprite') to show that rotating 90° then stretching vertically results in a different final pose than stretching then rotating.
